title: Optimizing Predictive Maintenance Thresholds
business: Industrial manufacturing firms managing high-speed assembly lines.
problem: Manual calibration of sensor sensitivity thresholds leads to excessive false-positive downtime alerts, incurring significant operational costs.
solution: Gradient Descent provides an iterative method to minimize the cost function representing the error between predicted and actual equipment failure states by adjusting threshold parameters in the direction opposite the gradient.
steps: Define a differentiable cost function that quantifies the error between predicted sensor alerts and actual maintenance events.
Calculate the gradient of the cost function with respect to the current threshold parameters.
Update the threshold parameters by moving in the direction of the negative gradient scaled by a chosen learning rate.
Repeat the iterative process until the cost function value reaches a sufficiently low level.
outcome: A refined set of sensor thresholds that minimizes false-positive alerts while maintaining high detection accuracy for genuine equipment failures.
limitation: The algorithm may converge to local minima that are not globally optimal; this is checked by comparing the final cost function value against different starting parameter initializations.
